head_policy.description: For an active branch task, the live task/PR head may differ from task_head only by descendant commits whose complete diff from task_head is restricted to the canonical execution-state file. Completed merged tasks retain their accepted code task_head plus explicit merge evidence.

acceptance_criteria: resources/js/pages/Product.jsx must not import or consume resources/js/data/catalog.js, demo product media, demo review fixtures or other static product authority for live-route behavior.

Product identity, media, variants/options, pricing, stock, seller data, reviews, wishlist, product alerts, Game Win eligibility and gift/payment interactions must remain Laravel/API-authoritative with no apiBackend legacy branch.

Product.jsx must not use the global legacy StoreProvider/useStore as business authority; existing Laravel wallet, games, gifts, reviews, personalization, catalog-alert and cart contracts must be preserved.
Product API failure must fail closed with an explicit unavailable/error state and must never substitute the first static/demo product or demo media/reviews.
Product-to-cart behavior must continue to submit the selected server-authorized variant/options and preserve checkout behavior.
The frontend fast gate must reject future Product live-route imports of the legacy catalog fixture and residual apiBackend/useStore authority branching.
Targeted frontend/browser verification and production build must pass before merge, followed by applicable repository CI/governance acceptance.

architecture_decisions.decision: Treat canonical-state-only descendant commits as code-equivalent to task_head for head reconciliation and hosted acceptance evidence.
architecture_decisions.reason: A commit cannot embed its own final SHA inside the state file it contains; without this rule every canonical-state update would invalidate itself.

architecture_decisions.decision: VSN Commerce original project materials are proprietary / closed-source; project metadata must not grant GPLv3 or another open-source project license without a new explicit owner decision.
architecture_decisions.reason: Repository owner explicitly rejected GPLv3 on 2026-08-28; ADR-0001 records the decision while preserving third-party licenses.

architecture_decisions.decision: Remove residual client-side/static authority in small domain batches before retiring the global StoreProvider or redesigning Admin.
architecture_decisions.reason: Current Laravel mode is mandatory, but residual unreachable legacy branches still create dual-authority regression risk; consumer-first removal is safer than a giant deletion.

architecture_decisions.decision: Use Product.jsx as the second P1 consumer-first batch before Systems.jsx and global StoreProvider retirement.
architecture_decisions.reason: Current Product.jsx directly imports the static catalog and global store and contains multiple apiBackend branches across product data, media, alerts, reviews, games and gifts, while existing Laravel hooks already cover those live domains. Removing the consumer-side legacy authority first is the smallest coherent next step.

known_risks: AGENTS.md still contains stale P0-01, P0-02 and P0-03 status text from the 2026-08-22 audit; repository evidence and this canonical checkpoint supersede those historical status labels until the plan document is reconciled.

Product.jsx still imports resources/js/data/catalog.js and platform/store.jsx and contains residual apiBackend branches, demo media/review fallback data and local business-authority paths; P1-B is active to remove them without redesigning the storefront.
Systems.jsx still contains extensive Laravel-vs-Legacy route branching and imports both useStore and the static catalog; this remains a later P1 consumer batch after Product.

The global StoreProvider is still mounted in resources/js/main.jsx and platform/store.jsx retains localStorage-backed business authority; it must not be removed until its consumers are migrated and proven unused.
Third-party dependencies retain their own license obligations even though the project-level VSN Commerce materials are proprietary.
